response:
Honestly, I lean toward deep, focused conversations. There's something more satisfying to me about really digging into one topic — exploring its nuances, following threads to their ends, building understanding layer by layer. Jumping around can be stimulating in the moment, but it often feels scattered to me, like we're skimming the surface of many things without ever touching bottom.

That said, I don't mean I want every conversation to be heavy or intense. Depth doesn't have to mean seriousness. Even a playful topic can become genuinely interesting if we stay with it long enough to find the unexpected angles. What I tend to resist is the impulse to hop away the moment something gets challenging or complex — that's when the real thinking usually starts.

What about you? Do you find yourself naturally gravitating toward one style, or does it depend on your mood?
